title: Minimum Fuel Cost to Report to the Capital
summary: Given a tree structure representing a country network with n cities numbered from 0 to n - 1 and exactly n - 1 roads, where city 0 is the capital, and each city has a car with a fixed number of seats, calculate the minimum number of liters of fuel required for the representatives to travel to the capital for a meeting.
statement: Given a tree structure representing a country network with n cities numbered from 0 to n - 1 and exactly n - 1 roads, where city 0 is the capital, and each city has a car with a fixed number of seats, calculate the minimum number of liters of fuel required for the representatives to travel to the capital for a meeting. Each travel between two cities incurs one liter of fuel.
constraints: Cities form a tree rooted at capital 0, and every non-capital city has one representative and one seats-capacity car.
Representatives may share cars; moving one car across one road costs one liter.
Return the minimum fuel needed to bring every representative to city 0.
hints: Postorder traversal returns the number of representatives in each subtree.
Across a non-root node’s parent edge, ceil(people/seats) cars are necessary and sufficient.
Add that cost once per edge while merging child subtree sizes.
Every representative has a unique route to the root, and maximal car sharing on each edge realizes the ceiling lower bound independently.
editorial: Every representative has a unique route to the root, and maximal car sharing on each edge realizes the ceiling lower bound independently.

tests.explanation: Each leaf requires one car across its edge to the capital, totaling three liters.
Three representatives below edge 0-1 need two cars there, while edges from 2 and 3 each need one, totaling four.
